18. NBB determines it needs to make a USMCA post-summary claim on a type 01 consumption entry filed on behalf of Echo. Of the following methods for making post-summary claims, which ONE cannot be used to make a post-summary claim under the USMCA?

A) File a post-summary claim under 19 USC 1520(d).
B) File a post-summary correction (PSC).
C) File a reconciliation entry as long as the originally filed entry was flagged for FTA reconcilation.
D) File a protest under 19 USC 1514 after the entry liquidates.

1. The entry summary processing in the ACE environment consists of three stages: under trade control, under CBP control, and liquidated.
2. After an entry summary is submitted in ACE and before the duty is collected by CBP, the entry summary is in trade control status. During this stage, the importer and broker can make any necessary modifications to the entry summary.
3. After the duty is collected and before liquidation, the entry summary is in CBP control status. During this stage, the importer and broker cannot make any changes to the entry summary. If modifications are necessary, they can file a Post Summary Correction (PSC).
4. After liquidation, the entry is considered final, and no changes can be made. If the importer disagrees with CBP's decision, they may file a request for reliquidation or a protest.
5. A protest is an action taken by the importer to dispute CBP's decision; it is not a proper method for making modifications to the entry summary. D is not the answer.
6. Reconciliation is a method that allows the importer to flag an issue that was uncertain when preparing the entry summary and reconcile it at a later time. The situation in question is not the case of reconciliation. C is not the answer. 
7. See Reconciliation External Guidance - B. 80. A mold for toys was provided free of charge to a French manufacturer by the U.S. importer. The original cost of the mold was $180,000 but 2/3 of the useful life of the mold had been used by the U.S. importer prior to sending it to France. The U.S. Importer paid the freight cost of $1,600. When calculating transaction value, what is the total value of the assist for the mold?

A) $0.00
B) $61,600.00
C) $180,000.00
D) $181,600.00

1. Transaction value is the price actually paid or payable plus additions to the price actually paid or payable. Assist is one of the additions.
2. Assist is the items provided by the buyer to the seller free of charge, used in the production of the imported merchandise.
3. If the item has been used before, depreciation should be considered when calculating the value of the assist. The cost of transporting the assist is also considered part of the assist if the buyer pays for the transportation.
4. See 152.103 (d) (2) If the assist consists of tools, dies, molds, or similar items used in the production of the imported merchandise, acquired by the buyer from an unrelated seller,the value of the assist is the cost of its acquisition. If the assist were produced by the buyer or a person related to the buyer, its value would be cost of its production. If the assist has been used previously by the buyer, regardless of whether it had been acquired or produced by him, the original cost of acquisition or production would be adjusted downward to reflect its use before its value could be determined. If the assist were leased by the buyer from an unrelated seller, the value of the assist would be the cost of the lease. In either case, the value of the assist would include transportation costs to the place of production. 
5. In this case, the original cost of the mold is $180,000, and 2/3 of the life of the mold has been used, the depreciated value is 1/3 of the original cost. So, the value of the assist is: $180,000 x 1/3 = $60,000. The transportation cost of $1,600 is paid by the buyer, it should be added to the assist value. So the total value of the assist is: $60,000 + $1,600 = $61,600.
6. B is the right answer.
